name: Tomevexa Book Catalog di Francesco La Mancusa
author: Francesco La Mancusa

sections.description:
Tomevexa Book Catalog di Francesco La Mancusa provides tools for creating and maintaining a book catalogue in WordPress.

Main features include:

  • A dedicated book post type and bibliographic taxonomies.
  • Searches and imports by ISBN, title, ASIN, or Amazon product URL.
  • Configurable bibliographic source: Open Library, Google Books, or Amazon Creators API.
  • Optional Amazon Creators API integration and Amazon Associates links.
  • Public author profiles with biography, dates, image attribution, and related books.
  • Catalogue, search, and single-book shortcodes.
  • Dynamic Gutenberg blocks for catalogue and book views.
  • Front-end output built with accessibility best practices in mind.

Imported books are saved as drafts so an editor can review them before publication.

External services

Tomevexa Book Catalog may communicate with the following external services when the related feature is used or enabled:

Google Books API

Used to search for and retrieve bibliographic data and cover information. Search terms, ISBNs, and book titles may be sent to Google. Google Books API terms: https://developers.google.com/books/terms — Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Open Library APIs

Used as a selectable source for bibliographic data and cover images. Search terms, ISBNs, and book titles may be sent to Open Library. The service is operated by the Internet Archive. Terms: https://archive.org/about/terms.php — Privacy policy: https://archive.org/about/terms.php#privacy

Amazon Creators API

Used only after the administrator configures valid credentials. ASINs, ISBNs, titles, and product requests may be sent to Amazon to retrieve product information and create supported affiliate links. Use is subject to Amazon’s applicable programme terms and privacy policy: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/agreement — https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=GX7NJQ4ZB8MHFRNJ

Wikimedia services

Wikidata, Wikipedia, and Wikimedia Commons may be queried to enrich author profiles with biographical information and properly attributed images. These requests occur only when an administrator explicitly chooses the author enrichment action from the author edit screen. The author name is then sent as a search term; no Wikimedia request is made automatically when an author term is created. Wikimedia services are operated by the Wikimedia Foundation. Terms: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use — Privacy policy: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Privacy_policy

Privacy

Bibliographic and author-enrichment requests are initiated by administrators or configured background jobs. Imported cover images are downloaded into the WordPress Media Library and are served locally on the public catalogue; external cover URLs are retained only as source metadata. Administrators should review the external-service terms and privacy policies and disclose enabled integrations as required for their site and jurisdiction.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the tomevexa-book-catalog folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP file from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate Tomevexa Book Catalog.
  3. Open Books > Settings and configure the catalogue and any optional external services.
  4. Open Books > Book Import to add books.
  5. Add the [tomevexa-book-catalog] shortcode to a page, or use one of the included blocks.
sections.faq:
Is an external account required?

No. Basic catalogue management works without an external account. Some import and enrichment functions depend on the external services described below.

Are imported books published automatically?

No. Newly imported books are saved as drafts for editorial review.

Does the plugin support Amazon affiliate links?

Yes. You can enter an Amazon Associates tracking ID in the plugin settings. Participation in the Amazon Associates programme is subject to Amazon’s terms.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Added administrator-selectable default bibliographic source for imports and book updates.
  • Removed automatic Google Books priority; Open Library, Google Books, and Amazon Creators API can be selected.
  • Clarified that the catalogue URL is administrator-managed and contains no fixed external address.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Added book catalogue management, Google Books imports, searches, author profiles, shortcodes, and blocks.
  • Added optional Amazon Creators API and Amazon Associates support.
  • Added Wikimedia-based author enrichment with source and licence attribution.
  • Added multisite support and accessible front-end templates.
